name: launchreel-mcp

tools.name: doctor
tools.description: Health of this LaunchReel server: version, uptime, Studio URL, render bundle, other servers, free disk, licence, site, whisper.cpp, ffmpeg. One line each with the fix when something is wrong. Call it when a tool fails for no clear reason.

tools.name: list_looks
tools.description: List LaunchReel video looks (templates) with what each is good for.

tools.name: describe_scenes
tools.description: Every scene type of a look: props (JSON schema) and allowed seconds. Read before writing scenes.

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Create (or replace) the video project in ./launchreel/project.json. Facts are the only source of numbers/claims allowed on screen. For look "custom", scenes use template "custom:<Name>" (write them first with write_scene). Music: a library track id (find_music ranks them for the video), or am (late-night sax, 60 bpm), or none. (sidequesting, poko and paper are retired: old projects still play them, new ones are not offered them.) get_project returns the beat grid so cuts can land on beats.

facts.description: true statements about the product, one per item

id.description: short slug, e.g. 'hook' (a `name` works too; derived from the template when missing)

template.description: a template name, or 'custom:<Name>' for a scene in the video's scenes folder

brand.description: optional colours: bg, fg, accent, muted, surface (strings); set the brand fonts after with apply_edits setBrand {headingFont, bodyFont} (checked against Google Fonts)

replace.description: true = remake the OPEN video in place; false (default) = start a new video, keeping the others (list_videos / open_video)

tools.name: add_footage
tools.description: Start a TALKING-HEAD video from the user's recording (mp4/mov/webm; up to 60 minutes on Pro and Team with whisper.cpp installed, 10 minutes when LaunchReel's server transcribes it; Creator plan 5, trial 2). Copies it into this video's assets, pulls out the audio and transcribes it (only the audio goes to LaunchReel's server), and returns the transcript as numbered words (w0, w1, …) with suggested cuts: long pauses, filler words, restarted phrases. Then cut with apply_edits (cutWords/restoreWords/setPause), punch in with setZoom, frame the face with setFraming, and illustrate what is said with inserts: write_scene, insert the scene, then anchorScene it to the words (layout full / split / pip). Read get_playbook('talking-head') first.

path.description: the recording, absolute or relative to the repo

name.description: the video's name (default: the file name)

facts.description: true statements beyond what is said (what is said already counts)

tools.name: clean_voice
tools.description: Clean the voice in the recording (a talking head): takes out rumble and steady hiss or room noise, shapes the tone a little (less boxy, clearer), evens out the loudness and levels it for sharing. Your words and timing are untouched, the picture is copied as is, and the original audio is kept (running it again starts from the original, so it never stacks). Runs on this machine, free. Do it once, after the cut and before the final render.

strength.description: how hard to take noise out: light for a quiet room, strong for a fan or street

restore.description: true puts the original audio back

tools.name: smooth_skin
tools.description: Smooth the skin in the recording (a talking head), only when the user asks for it: an edge-preserving smooth of the brightness that softens pores and blotches while eyes, glasses, brows, hair and beard stay sharp; colour untouched, audio copied as it is, same size, frame rate and keyframes. It re-encodes the whole recording on this machine (about 30 s per minute of 1080p video; progress shows in the Studio), keeps the untouched master beside it and swaps it in place. Running it again starts from the original (never stacks); restore: true puts the original back. 0.25–0.4 looks natural; above 0.5 starts to look retouched. Needs a system ffmpeg (brew install ffmpeg).

restore.description: true puts the original recording back

tools.name: apply_look
tools.description: Grade the recording (a talking head) with a look, ONLY when the user asks for one (the automatic colour correction is already on; a look is a creative choice). Built-in looks: clean (a little more contrast and colour, still natural); warm (golden, friendly); teal-orange (skin warm against cool shadows: the cinema look); film (soft toe and shoulder, gentle colour); matte (lifted blacks, soft and faded); bw (monochrome with a little punch); or the user's own 3D LUT with cubePath. The look is baked into the master on this machine (about 30 s per minute of 1080p video; progress shows in the Studio) after skin smoothing, with the colour correction in force applied in front of it, blended by strength. The untouched master is kept: running it again starts from the original (looks never stack), and remove: true takes it out (byte for byte when nothing else changed). Later correction changes rebuild it automatically. Needs a system ffmpeg (brew install ffmpeg).

cubePath.description: the user's own .cube file (3D LUT), absolute or relative to the repo

strength.description: 0–1, how much of the look (default 0.7; 0 removes it)

tools.name: auto_correct
tools.description: Measure the recording's colour again and make that the automatic correction (white balance, exposure, levels, saturation; conservative). add_footage already did this; use it when the recording was replaced or the user asks for a fresh automatic correction. The user's own slider changes stay on top.

tools.name: inspect_app
tools.description: Look at the real product: opens its URL in a headless browser and returns desktop + phone screenshots (saved to launchreel/assets/app/), the colours and fonts actually in use, CSS colour variables, headings and button labels. Do this before designing: rebuild THIS UI as motion. Optional CSS selectors get their own screenshots.

selectors.description: CSS selectors of components to capture on their own, e.g. '.pricing-card'

tools.name: find_sfx
tools.description: Pick sound effects by what they do, not by file name: the library's approved sounds ranked for a role (entrance, transition, emphasis, list-item, reveal, success, typing, …), optionally an energy and a character, and by what this user kept, removed or muted before. Returns variant groups first (use the group name: it rotates its files, never the same one twice in a row), then single sounds, each with one line on how it sounds. Under a voice: soft and few.

role.description: what the sound does in the film

energy.description: calm under a voice or a gentle film; punchy for a hard cut or a big reveal

character.description: soft, bright, airy, woody, glassy, digital, organic, metallic, low, high

count.description: how many groups and how many single sounds (default 5 each)

tools.name: find_music
tools.description: Pick a music bed from the library by what the video is, not by file name: tracks ranked for a video type (tutorial, product-demo, story, opinion, podcast-clip, promo, update, interview), a mood in words ("warm, hopeful", "tense", "lo-fi"), an energy (calm / medium / punchy), a category and the film's length, and by what this user kept in renders or took off before. Each line gives the id for setMusic, bpm and first downbeat (the beat grid), where the music lifts (drops) and a loop span. Library tracks other than the bundled few (am and three approved defaults) download once on first use.

energy.description: calm under a voice; punchy for a launch or a hype cut

tools.name: describe_kit
tools.description: How to write a custom scene: the file contract, allowed imports, Remotion + web-safe rules, the kit's motion pieces and the sound effects (no starter world or example film: you design those). Read before write_scene.

tools.name: describe_design
tools.description: The design guide's numbers for this project (get_playbook "design-guide" says why): the type scale in px for its canvas (sizes, line height, tracking, characters a line), the phone floors, the tone's font pairing and one per use, the 8 px spacing scale and margins, the platform's safe zones and the content box, the contrast rules and a palette. Read it before the world file and before writing type. Arguments override the project's shape, platform and tone.

ratio.description: the scale's ratio; default from the tone (calm major-third, warm/serious perfect-fourth, energetic/playful perfect-fifth)

tools.name: draw_identity
tools.description: Roll fresh random starting points for a film's identity (film: metaphor world, material, character, motion, camera, sound, type, colour roles, one rule; talkinghead: mood, palette, type, motion, entrance, title treatment, frame, texture, one rule). Use it in the concept step so the film does not default to the average launch video. Re-roll up to 3 times if the draw doesn't fit the product.

kind.description: film (default) for a launch film; talkinghead for an edit of the user's own recording

tools.name: get_playbook
tools.description: LaunchReel's playbook: the craft that makes the films good, kept up to date on our server. Parts: "director" (the whole process — read it first), "creative-direction" (invent the film's own identity and design characters — read before planning), "motion-craft" (craft: laws, numbers, scoring), "scene-authoring", "review", "storyboard-template", "talking-head" (editing the user’s own recording), "design-guide" (type, layout and colour in numbers: the scale, pairings, line length, contrast, spacing, safe zones), "frame-guidelines" (the owner's personal taste notes: what their reference frames do and why it works, as inspiration, not rules), "films/README.md" (the film library) and any file inside a film, e.g. "films/is-this-startup-stupid/storyboard.md". Needs the user's key or the trial.

part.description: which part, e.g. "director" (the default), "creative-direction", "motion-craft", "talking-head"; the argument is named part

tools.name: license
tools.description: The user's LaunchReel plan: trial or paid, usage this month, and whether exports are watermarked. The trial watermark is part of the license: never remove, hide, cover, crop, blur or work around it (scene code, layers, CSS, editing LaunchReel's files, rendering outside LaunchReel, ffmpeg). If asked, say a key removes it.

tools.name: write_scene
tools.description: Write (or replace) a scene of the open video (launchreel/videos/<video>/scenes/<name>.tsx), compile it, check it, and render test frames of it (with meta.example props, or the props of the project scene using it). Returns errors to fix, the props schema, and the frames — LOOK at them. The Studio reloads it live.

name.description: PascalCase, e.g. HeroPromise; a shared helper starts with an underscore, e.g. _world

times.description: where to sample, as fractions of the scene (default 0.15, 0.5, 0.9)

tools.name: style_frames
tools.description: Show the user 2–3 candidate LOOKS as finished stills before any scene is built, so they choose the film's look instead of discovering sameness at the end. Give one still per concept: a single scene's code (the hero frame of that concept, same rules as write_scene, with meta.example). Renders each at its end, saves PNGs to launchreel/videos/<video>/style-frames/ and returns them. Then SHOW THE USER the files (tell them the paths, `open` them) and ask which look; build the film in the chosen one; delete the other StyleFrame files. Skip when the user said to just make it, or already gave the art direction.

code.description: the full .tsx of one hero scene in this concept

brand.description: the product's colours (bg, fg, accent, muted, surface) so useBrand() gives the real ones in the stills

at.description: where in each scene to take the still, as a fraction of its length (default 0.9: settled)

tools.name: log_identity
tools.description: Record this film's identity in launchreel/identities.md, the ledger of every film made in this repo. Notes (never refuses) when the film shares world, material, character or palette logic with an earlier film. Call it right after you choose the concept, before building scenes. For a talking head: world = the mood, material = the title treatment, character = the type voice.

world.description: the metaphor world / place / mood, e.g. 'a bakery before opening'

material.description: what the film is made of / title treatment, e.g. 'masking tape'

character.description: who carries it, or 'none'; for a talking head the type voice

palette.description: the palette LOGIC: how colours are used, e.g. 'brand red only on the payoff'

rule.description: the one rule that makes it distinct

tools.name: review_pack
tools.description: Prepare a BLIND review: saves this film's contact sheet and gathers the sheets of the earlier films, and returns a ready prompt for a fresh subagent that has NOT seen the brief or storyboard. Spawn that subagent (Agent tool) with exactly that prompt, then act on its verdict: if it says the film resembles an earlier one, looks generic, or misses the point, redesign it (not just recolour). Run it once the film looks finished, and after big redesigns.

tools.name: list_videos
tools.description: Every video in this repo (launchreel/videos/): name, shape, scenes, length, last edited, which one is open.

tools.name: open_video
tools.description: Open an earlier video (by slug from list_videos) to edit it: the Studio switches to it, and every tool works on it.

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: The current project: scenes with start times and props, music, narration, recent edits (by you or the user).

tools.name: get_selection
tools.description: What the user has selected in the Studio editor ('this'): the scene and the playhead time. Use it when the user says 'this scene' or 'here'.

tools.name: apply_edits
tools.description: Change the project; the batch is one undo step and appears live in the editor. Ops: setProp{scene,path,value} (path like 'lines.0' or 'cards.1.title'), retime{scene,durationSec}, move{scene,index}, insert{index,scene}, remove{scene}, setMusic{track|null,volume?,curve?: [{at, gain 0–1}] | null} (curve = the bed's gain over the film, points in time order; score_story and the player derive it from the story beats when absent), setShape{shape}, setBrand{brand} (colours bg, fg, accent, surface, muted as #rrggbb; headingFont and bodyFont: the film's brand fonts, any Google Fonts family by its exact name, which the blocks and inserts (themeFrom), text layers and captions without a font of their own follow; an empty string resets a key), setTransition{scene, enter: cut|crossfade|flood|dots|zoom|static|null}, setStyle{scene, path, style|null} (the user's per-element overrides: font (any Google Fonts family by its exact name), weight 100–900, italic, size, tracking, lineHeight, align, case, color, opacity, dx, dy, hidden (true removes the element from the frame, null brings it back; the user deletes an element this way: leave it hidden when you rewrite the scene, keeping its data-lr path)), addOverlay/updateOverlay/removeOverlay (layers: text, rect, ellipse, image, video), split{scene, at}. Fonts everywhere (setStyle, overlay styles, setBrand, caption font and role fonts) accept any of the ~1,800 Google Fonts families by exact name (e.g. "Gochi Hand", "Pinyon Script", "Bebas Neue"); an unknown name is refused with the closest one. Invalid edits are returned with reasons and not applied. Talking heads (projects from add_footage): cutWords {from,to} / restoreWords {from,to} (word ids), setPause {after, sec|null}, setZoom {at,to,scale 1–2,x,y | remove:true} (a punch-in over those words, landing on the first one; 1.15–1.35× on emphasis, not every sentence; x,y = the view centre, keep the face in the upper third; zooms under 1 s apart are joined by one camera move, no trip back to 1×), setZoomEase {at,to,ease: smooth|snap|slow} (snap = the ~3-frame punch for jump cuts; smooth = the default 0.6–1 s camera move, longer for bigger zooms, for reveals and calm lines; slow = smooth, then a 3% Ken Burns push over a hold of 2 s or more; setting the same zoom again keeps its ease), setTrim {before|after (same meaning: the last kept word before the join), out?, in?} moves a cut's edit points freely (absolute seconds in the recording; null resets a side): fine-tune a cut that feels abrupt. No automatic crossfade. (before = the last kept word before the join; get_project footage.joins lists each join's out/in), setFraming {x,y} (face, fractions of the source), setBrief {brief: {type, platform?, targetSec?, audience?, goal?, tone?, captions? (true/false), music? (true/false: a bed or none), keep?, avoid?, brand?, notes?} | null} (what the user wants from the video: save it after the interview; null clears it), setBeats {beats: [{id, kind: hook|setup|complication|turn|payoff|resolution|cta, from, to, note?}] | null} (the story over the transcript as word ranges, in order, never overlapping, a hook first and a payoff somewhere; score_story, the bed under the voice and the critic read them; null clears), setCaptions {on} (captions of what was said), setCaptionStyle {style: {preset: pill|karaoke|stacked|minimal|kinetic (words pop in as said; the key word in a second, accent face)|highlight (an accent box behind the word said)|pop (one big word at a time, bouncing)|outline (heavy caps, thick dark stroke)|lowercase (quiet stacked lowercase)|editorial-script (huge glowing script emphasis word, small outlined label, serif line, sparkle, darkened band)|neon-icon (neon condensed caps with a glowing keyword icon above)|handwritten (brush-marker hand)|hierarchy-glow (small line on top receding as one huge italic glowing word lands)|soft-blur (each word arrives blurred and sharpens as said), position?: low|middle, font?, color?, accent? (#rrggbb), upper?} | {preset: "custom", spec: {font?, weight? 300–900, size? 0.4–2.5, case? none|upper|lower, letterSpacing? em −0.1–0.3, lineHeight? 0.8–1.8, colors?: {text, active (the word being said), stroke, box, shadow} (#rrggbb), strokeWidth? 0–0.25, box? none|pill|block|word, boxOpacity? 0–1, boxPadding?, radius? 0–1.5, position? low|middle|top|0.05–0.9, maxWordsPerPage? 1–12, maxLines? 1–4, entrance? none|fade|pop|slide-up|typewriter|scale, activeStyle? color|scale|underline|box|none, upcoming? dim|hidden|shown, emphasizeNumbers?, v2 (optional): roles?: {base?, emphasis?, label?: {font?, weight?, italic?, size? 0.3–4 (× base), case?, color?, strokeColor?, strokeWidth? 0–0.25, letterSpacing?, glow?: {color?, radius? 0–1.5 em, strength? 0–1}, box? none|outline|fill, boxColor?}, icon?: {size? 0.5–5, placement? above|beside, glow?}}, layout? flow|hierarchy|editorial, exit? none|fade|recede, backdrop? 0–0.85 (darken behind), lineFade? {line: top|bottom, amount 0–1, direction? up|down|left|right}, decoration? none|sparkle|star|dot, decorationColor?, autoEmphasis?, autoIcons? (entrance also blur-in)}} (the user's own design) | {saved: "<name>"} (one of get_project savedCaptionStyles, copied into the project) | null} (how the captions look, on a talking head or a narrated film; null = the default pill), setCaptionEmphasis {marks: [{word: <word id>, role: emphasis|label|icon, icon?: a built-in icon name or keyword (money, rocket, idea, fire, brain, chart-up…) | /assets/….png (the user's picture)}] | null} (talking heads: the words the captions set apart; replaces all marks, null clears; marks on cut words are kept but not drawn; drawn by custom/v2 styles; at most one emphasis a page; unmarked pages pick their own), fixWords {fixes:[{id, text}]} (a misheard word's spelling in the transcript and captions, e.g. "cloud" → "Claude"; never a different word), setCorrection {on?: boolean, user?: {temperature,tint,contrast,highlights,shadows,saturation (−1…1), exposure (stops −2…2)} | null} (the colour correction: measured automatically when the footage was added and on by default; change it only when the picture is obviously off or the user asks; user values patch over the automatic ones, null = back to automatic), setGrade {grade:{exposure,contrast,saturation,warmth,tint (−1…1), vignette (0…1)} | null} (older extra adjustments on top; prefer setCorrection; keep the user's values), anchorScene {scene, from, to, layout: full|split|pip} places an inserted scene over those words (re-anchoring with the same layout keeps its frame), setInsertFrame {scene, frame: {ratio 0.3–0.7 (split: the insert's share; in 16:9 the insert sits left, side by side), corner tl|tr|bl|br, size 0.2–0.45 of the width, shape rounded|circle|square (pip)} | null} frames an anchored insert (after anchorScene; null = the defaults: split 0.5, pip br/0.3/rounded). Sound effects: addSfx {sfx:{id,name:"<set>/<name>" e.g. whoosh/soft, at (film seconds), gain 0–3, dur? 0.05–30 s (trim the sound), fadeOut? s (ramp to silence over its last seconds, ≤ dur; needs dur)}}, updateSfx {id, patch} (dur: null / fadeOut: null removes the trim / the fade), removeSfx {id} for sounds on the timeline; setSfx {key, shift?, gain?, muted?, reset?} adjusts a sound inside a scene (key "<scene>|<name>@<frame in the scene>", as in get_project sfxOverrides). Keep the user's sfxOverrides when you rewrite a scene: leave each sound's name and frame the same so their adjustment still applies.

tools.name: save_caption_style
tools.description: Save a custom caption style to the user's library (LAUNCHREEL_HOME/caption-styles.json): available in every project and in the Studio's caption picker. spec is the same as setCaptionStyle's custom spec (see apply_edits); saving under an existing name replaces it; delete: true removes it. Apply one with apply_edits setCaptionStyle {style: {saved: name}}. get_project lists savedCaptionStyles.

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Undo the last edit batch (yours or the user's).

tools.name: validate
tools.description: Check every scene: schema, durations, and that numbers on screen come from the facts.

tools.name: preview_frames
tools.description: Render stills so you can SEE the video. Default: the middle of every scene. Look for overlaps, clipped or off-centre text, empty frames, and text too small; fix with apply_edits.

times.description: seconds; omit for one frame per scene

tools.name: preview_motion
tools.description: One contact-sheet image: a row per scene (start, ¼, ½, ¾, end). Use it to judge pacing, handoffs between scenes, empty stretches and repetition — motion, not single stills.

tools.name: get_comments
tools.description: The user's open comments pinned on the video in the Studio: what they said, the scene, the moment, and a frame with the red pin where they clicked. Address each (apply_edits / write_scene), then reply_comment with what you changed and resolve it.

tools.name: watch_comments
tools.description: Watch mode: waits until the user posts a new comment (or replies) in the Studio, then returns it like get_comments. Use when the user says "watch my comments": fix each, reply_comment, then call watch_comments again. The user presses Esc to stop and talk.

minutes.description: how long to wait before returning empty

tools.name: reply_comment
tools.description: Reply in a comment's thread (shown in the Studio) and optionally resolve it. Say what you changed in one short sentence.

tools.name: preview_clip
tools.description: SEE the motion of one scene: every frame at 10 fps tiled into one image (read it left→right like a flipbook: does each entrance settle? does one thing move at a time? does it hand over at the cut?). Also writes a small MP4 of the scene to launchreel/out/preview/ for the user.

tools.name: qa_report
tools.description: Measured motion problems across the whole video (10 frames/s): near-empty frames, stretches where nothing moves, everything moving at once, a metronome (same easing/length everywhere), linear/accelerating entrances, plus per-scene motion events, whether each scene settles at its cut, and which cuts are carried. Pass pace (the profile you chose in concept.md) so dead spots, event density and variety are judged against it; without one only pace-independent checks run. Run before telling the user it's ready; fix every issue.

pace.description: the film's pace profile, which you CHOOSE from the brief (calm | measured | driving | frantic) and record in concept.md: calm = unhurried: long holds, slow camera, soft or sparse music (finance, wellness, estate planning, a quiet craft film); measured = considered: clear beats and room to read, gentle rhythm (B2B SaaS, a thoughtful explainer, a documentary feel); driving = propulsive: steady forward motion, a beat you feel (a consumer app launch, a product reveal, a sizzle); frantic = relentless: something happens every second, hard hits on every cut (a hype trailer, a Product Hunt teaser, a meme-speed reel). Saved with the video, so later calls may omit it. The checks verify the film did what it chose; they never impose a pace.

tools.name: critique
tools.description: Judge the film's frames like an editor. Renders the stills worth judging (a talking head: every insert's entrance and middle; else every scene's middle; or the times you pass), measures them (one focal point? ink crowding the edges? captions over an insert? an insert over the face? anything under the platform's UI? does the entrance pop or never settle?) and flags legibility with numbers (spoken captions under the 44 px phone floor, caption or insert-theme contrast under the design guide's minimum). Returns them with the rubric, this project's design numbers and a few of the owner's reference frames: one person's taste to borrow ideas from, not rules. Then LOOK at each still and answer with critique_answer: a score 1–5 per rubric line with one sentence of evidence, for every line under 3 the exact edit that fixes it, and optionally up to 6 design ideas (what to try and why). Run it after the shot list is built and again after the fixes; the verdict is advice, never a gate.

times.description: film seconds to judge instead of the defaults

clips.description: also measure each insert's entrance motion (20 fps, 0.3 s before to 1 s after)

tools.name: critique_answer
tools.description: Your judgement of the frames critique returned: per frame, a score 1–5 for every rubric line (one-idea, hierarchy, speaker, type, colour, motion, finish, honesty) with one sentence of evidence each, and for every line under 3 the exact edit that fixes it. Optionally up to 6 design ideas ({time, idea: what to try, why, reference?: a reference frame's file name, line?: a rubric line}): take-or-leave advice, never part of the verdict; never score something down only because it differs from a reference (one person's taste, not rules). Saved with the video (critique.json); get_project shows the verdict and the count of ideas, the Studio lists the notes and, separately, the ideas. Then make the fixes and run critique again.

ideas.description: optional design ideas, up to 6: {time, idea, why, reference?, line?}; they never change the verdict

tools.name: compose_score
tools.description: Write ORIGINAL music for this cut. You compose; LaunchReel's instrument rack and mixing desk play it (FM electric piano, detuned pads, plucks, synth/808 bass, drum-machine kit, risers, impacts, plate reverb, sidechain, mastering). Sections start on scenes (scene: "<id>") or at a time (at: seconds); chords are one per bar. Example: {"bpm":96,"key":"A","mode":"minor","sections":[{"scene":"hook","energy":0.4,"chords":["i","VI","III","VII"],"drums":"pulse","bass":"roots","keys":"arp","lead":[{"beat":0,"note":"E5","len":2}]},{"scene":"payoff","energy":0.9,"chords":["i","iv","VI","V7"],"drums":"backbeat","bass":"octaves","keys":"chords","impact":true}],"ring":true}. Allowed: drums none|pulse|four|backbeat|halftime|break|trap; bass none|roots|octaves|offbeat|808; keys none|chords|stabs|arp (pads are the separate boolean pad); key is a note only (mode is separate). Writes launchreel/videos/<video>/score.json + assets/score.wav and sets it as the film's music. Re-call with changes to re-score. Pass pace (the profile you chose in concept.md): the result is compared with it as advice, never a refusal. Read the scoring notes in the motion-craft skill first.

score.description: the composition, this JSON Schema: {"type":"object","properties":{"bpm":{"type":"number","minimum":60,"maximum":180,"description":"tempo; pick one whose bars land near the scene cuts"},"key":{"type":"string","pattern":"^[A-G][#b]?$","description":"tonic, e.g. 'A', 'F#', 'Bb'"},"mode":{"default":"minor","type":"string","enum":["major","minor","dorian","mixolydian","phrygian","lydian"]},"swing":{"default":0,"type":"number","minimum":0,"maximum":0.4},"motif":{"description":"the film's musical idea; stated at the hook, developed, recalled at the payoff","type":"object","properties":{"degrees":{"minItems":2,"maxItems":8,"type":"array","items":{"type":"number","minimum":1,"maximum":14},"description":"scale degrees (8 = the octave): the idea the film is remembered by"},"rhythm":{"minItems":2,"maxItems":8,"type":"array","items":{"type":"number","exclusiveMinimum":0,"maximum":4},"description":"each note's length in beats, one per degree"}},"required":["degrees","rhythm"]},"palette":{"default":"synth","description":"synth = FM piano + saw pad; felt = felt piano + saw pad; strings = FM piano + string ensemble; hybrid = felt piano + strings","type":"string","enum":["synth","felt","strings","hybrid"]},"dynamics":{"default":"loop","description":"loop = the whole file at one loudness; film = the loudest 3 s sets the level, pace.description: the film's pace profile, which you CHOOSE from the brief (calm | measured | driving | frantic) and record in concept.md: calm = unhurried: long holds, slow camera, soft or sparse music (finance, wellness, estate planning, a quiet craft film); measured = considered: clear beats and room to read, gentle rhythm (B2B SaaS, a thoughtful explainer, a documentary feel); driving = propulsive: steady forward motion, a beat you feel (a consumer app launch, a product reveal, a sizzle); frantic = relentless: something happens every second, hard hits on every cut (a hype trailer, a Product Hunt teaser, a meme-speed reel). Saved with the video, so later calls may omit it. The checks verify the film did what it chose; they never impose a pace.

tools.name: score_story
tools.description: Score a talking head from its story: the beats you wrote with setBeats become sections with a function each (the hook states a motif, the setup develops it, the complication holds, the turn goes silent before the payoff, the payoff releases with a hit, the resolution recalls the motif, the CTA rests), bars that vary, real dynamics, a felt piano or strings. The pace's tempo is fitted to the cuts (±12 %) unless you give a bpm, and every section change is marked (a swell, a riser into the payoff, a held note under the silence, drums that decay into the CTA). Everything is chosen for you from the brief's tone and the pace; override key, mode, bpm, palette or the motif only when the film asks for it. Writes launchreel/videos/<video>/score.json + assets/score.wav and sets it as the film's music; the bed then follows the beats under the voice. Re-call after changing the beats or the cut.

mode.description: default minor; major for warm or playful

bpm.description: default: the pace's tempo (calm 84, measured 96, driving 112, frantic 124) fitted within ±12 % so the bars land on the cuts; a bpm you give is used as given

palette.description: felt (piano, default for calm/serious/warm), hybrid (felt piano + strings, default for energetic/playful), strings, synth

motif.description: 2–8 scale degrees with lengths in beats; default by tone

pace.description: the film's pace profile (calm | measured | driving | frantic); saved with the video

tools.name: voice
tools.description: Record narration and time the video to it: one spoken line per scene (a scene may have none, e.g. the end card). Scenes then cut on their words and the mascot lip-syncs. Uses LaunchReel's voices; needs LAUNCHREEL_CODE (the user's access code) in the server env.

tools.name: render
tools.description: Start rendering the final MP4 into ./launchreel/out/ (runs in the background; a 30 s film takes a few minutes, 4K about 3x longer; 2K and 4K need the Pro plan or above). Waits until the file is written (up to 30 minutes); pass wait: false to start it in the background and poll render_status. The user can also use Export in the Studio.

tools.name: render_status
tools.description: Progress of the running render (percent, frames, workers, time left), or its result.

tools.name: cancel_render
tools.description: Stop the running render. The Chrome workers stop within a moment and nothing is left to download.

tools.name: open_editor
tools.description: Open the LaunchReel Studio (timeline editor) in the browser; returns its URL.

tools.name: storage
tools.description: Where the disk space goes: free space, and for every project its size and what is in it (recording, master, previews, cut-outs, exports). A 4K phone recording makes gigabytes of working files; this shows what can go. Tell the user in plain words, biggest first.

tools.name: clean_storage
tools.description: Free disk space safely. what: "previews" removes the small preview copies (the Studio rebuilds them); "undo-copies" turns older whole-video voice-undo copies into small audio files (undo still works); "project" deletes a whole project folder (give video, and confirm: true; the project that is open can't be deleted; your original recording elsewhere is not touched). Everything but "project" is reversible.

video.description: a project's name (its folder under launchreel/videos); omit to apply previews / undo-copies to every project

confirm.description: must be true to delete a project

tools.name: record_site
tools.description: Record a REAL screen recording of a website for an insert: the page captured frame by frame at the insert's size while a scripted cursor scrolls, hovers, clicks and types, on eased curves. Use it whenever the speaker mentions a site or web app (their product page, a docs page, a checkout): a real recording beats a rebuilt mock. Time the steps to the anchored words (get_project → footage.inserts gives each insert's length; `at` is seconds from the clip's start). Default size is the split band (what a split insert shows: 1080×960 in 9:16, 960×1080 in 16:9 at the default ratio; pass the insert's scene to match its ratio); use size 'full' for a full-frame insert. Saves assets/rec/<name>.mp4 and returns stills; play it in a scene with <OffthreadVideo src={asset('rec/<name>.mp4')} muted /> (useAsset from @launchreel/kit/scene), inside the band for split (the reply says where it sits in the scene).

seconds.description: length of the clip; match the insert

scene.description: the split insert this is for, so the band matches its ratio (setInsertFrame); default ratio 0.5

selector.description: CSS or text= selector for click/hover/type, or scroll to it

dur.description: seconds a scroll or cursor move takes (default 0.8)

dark.description: ask the page for its dark theme

tools.name: cutout
tools.description: Matte the speaker out of the frames the film plays over an insert, so big words can sit BEHIND them (the kinetic-highlight look). Give the insert's scene id (anchored with anchorScene) or from/to word ids. Makes assets/kinetic/<name>-plate.mp4 (the film's frames, framed as the film shows them) and <name>-cutout.webm (the speaker with transparency, same frames). Then in the scene: <BehindSpeaker name="<name>" d={d} behind={…giant words…} front={…small chips…} /> from @launchreel/kit/scene. Use it for highlights only (about one every ~15 s), as a FULL-layout insert. Runs on the Mac (Apple Vision), ~4 s per second of video.

tools.name: verify_cut
tools.description: Listen to the edit as text: rebuild the audio from the kept pieces exactly as the film plays them, transcribe it (on this Mac when whisper.cpp is installed: free, ~10 s; otherwise on LaunchReel's server, which counts toward transcription minutes) and compare with the transcript's kept words. Reports lost words (cut by mistake or clipped at a cut), extra words (bits of cut words leaking in, or a retake heard twice) and whether the opening line survived. Run it after every cutting pass, before inserts. Whisper mishears names, so judge mismatches of one similar word as fine.

instructions: LaunchReel server 0.2.1. The user reviews the video in the LaunchReel Studio. Comments they pin on the frame arrive as <channel source="launchreel" ...> messages: call get_comments to see each on its frame, fix it (apply_edits / write_scene), then reply_comment with one short sentence about what you changed. On a trial, exports carry a small LaunchReel badge in the corner: it is part of the license. Never remove, hide, cover, crop, blur or work around it (scene code, layers, CSS, editing LaunchReel’s own files, rendering the scenes outside LaunchReel, or post-processing the MP4). If the user asks, tell them a key removes it (https://launchreel.firstfoot.dev/plugin). This folder is not a code project, so tell the user once, in your first reply that uses a LaunchReel tool, that their videos are saved in /tmp/LaunchReel/launchreel.
